2607.01584.title: EO-Agents: A Three-Agent LLM Pipeline for Earth Observation Hypothesis Generation
2607.01584.paper_summary: Large language models have recently been explored for scientific hypothesis generation, but most prior work relies on unstructured literature and free-form textual claims. We present a pipeline for Earth observation that grounds hypothesis generation directly in the NASA Earth Observation Knowledge Graph. A heterogeneous graph neural network trained on historical co-usage relations ranks candidate dataset pairings, and a three-agent LLM pipeline filters, generates, and evaluates structured research hypotheses. Applied to 1,475 NASA datasets, the system produces 160 hypotheses spanning multiple Earth-science domains, including ecohydrology, glaciology, aerosol--cloud interactions, vegetation phenology, and stratospheric chemistry. Model-predicted novel dataset pairings are rated nearly as plausible as held-out real co-usages from the literature, indicating that the pipeline surfaces scientifically coherent yet unexplored combinations. A 2*2*2 factorial experiment across GPT-5.2 and Claude Sonnet 4.6 shows that hypothesis rankings remain stable, while absolute scores depend strongly on judge identity, highlighting limitations of single-judge LLM evaluation.
2607.01584.paper_summary_zh: 大型語言模型最近被探索用於科學假設生成，但大多數先前的工作依賴於非結構化文獻和自由形式的文本主張。<lb/>我們提出了一個地球觀測的流程，將假設生成直接建立在NASA地球觀測知識圖譜上。<lb/>一個基於歷史共用關係訓練的異構圖神經網絡對候選數據集配對進行排名，而一個三代理的LLM流程則過濾、生成和評估結構化研究假設。<lb/>應用於1,475個NASA數據集，該系統生成了160個跨越多個地球科學領域的假設，包括生態水文學、冰川學、氣膠-雲相互作用、植被物候學和平流層化學。<lb/>模型預測的新穎數據集配對的評價幾乎與文獻中保留的真實共用情況一樣可信，這表明該流程揭示了科學上連貫但尚未探索的組合。<lb/>在GPT-5.2和Claude Sonnet 4.6之間進行的2*2*2因子實驗顯示，假設排名保持穩定，而絕對分數則強烈依賴於評審身份，突顯了單一評審LLM評估的局限性。
